claims.claim: Claude Code supports 4 scope levels for skills with priority order Enterprise > Personal (~/.claude/skills/) > Project (.claude/skills/) > Plugin (namespaced as plugin-name:skill-name).
claims.evidence: Official table at code.claude.com/docs/en/skills with exact scope paths; quote 'higher-priority locations win: enterprise > personal > project'.

claims.claim: Plugin skills use a plugin-name:skill-name namespace and cannot conflict with other scope levels.
claims.evidence: Quote from code.claude.com/docs/en/skills: 'Plugin skills use a plugin-name:skill-name namespace, so they cannot conflict with other levels.'

claims.claim: In Claude Code 2.1+, custom commands (.claude/commands/) and skills (.claude/skills/) are merged; when both exist with same name, the skill takes precedence.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence'.

claims.claim: Progressive disclosure is a 3-level architecture: Level 1 metadata (~100 tokens/skill, always loaded), Level 2 instructions (<5k tokens, loaded on trigger), Level 3 resources (unlimited, loaded via bash read).
claims.evidence: Official table platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview with token cost columns.

claims.claim: Anthropic engineering blog reports total startup overhead ~1,500 tokens for 40 skills via progressive disclosure.
claims.evidence: Eng blog: 'With progressive disclosure, the overhead is roughly 1,500 tokens total for all 40 skills'.

claims.claim: Frontmatter has 13 officially documented fields: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, hooks, paths, shell (all optional; only description recommended).
claims.evidence: Official frontmatter reference table code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.

claims.claim: Agent Skills API spec enforces: name max 64 chars lowercase/numbers/hyphens only, description max 1024 chars, no XML tags, reserved words 'anthropic' and 'claude' forbidden in name.
claims.evidence: Agent Skills spec platform.claude.com validation rules.

claims.claim: Claude Code truncates combined (description + when_to_use) to 1536 characters per entry in skill listing; skill listing budget scales dynamically to 1% of context window with fallback 8000 chars, overridable via SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET env var.
claims.evidence: Troubleshooting section code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.

claims.claim: After auto-compaction, Claude Code re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill keeping first 5,000 tokens; total re-attached skills share 25,000 tokens combined budget; older skills may be dropped entirely.
claims.evidence: Content lifecycle section code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.

claims.claim: Three invocation paths exist: (a) automatic description-match (Claude decides), (b) manual /skill-name (user slash), (c) Skill tool programmatic (agents/skills can invoke).
claims.evidence: Official invocation paths section code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.

claims.claim: disable-model-invocation:true removes skill description from system prompt (token savings) and blocks all automatic/programmatic invocation; skill remains accessible only via manual /name.
claims.evidence: Official behavior table: 'disable-model-invocation:true -> Description NOT in context, full skill on user invoke'.

claims.claim: user-invocable:false hides skill from / slash menu but does NOT block Skill tool programmatic access; description remains in context.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'The user-invocable field only controls menu visibility, not Skill tool access. Use disable-model-invocation:true to block programmatic invocation.'

claims.claim: Permission rules for Skill tool support: Skill (deny all), Skill(name) (exact), Skill(name *) (prefix), Skill(name *) in deny (block specific).
claims.evidence: Restrict Claude skill access section code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.

claims.claim: Five string substitution variables available in skill content: $ARGUMENTS (full), $ARGUMENTS[N]/$N (indexed), ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}.
claims.evidence: String substitutions section official docs.

claims.claim: Dynamic context injection via !`command` executes BEFORE skill content enters context; output replaces placeholder; disableable via settings 'disableSkillShellExecution':true.
claims.evidence: Dynamic context injection section docs; security note.

claims.claim: context:fork creates isolated subagent context; requires agent field (e.g., Explore, Plan, general-purpose); SKILL.md becomes prompt; main session receives summary.
claims.evidence: Subagent integration section docs; warning: 'context:fork only makes sense for skills with explicit instructions'.

claims.claim: Live change detection: Claude Code watches skill directories and applies add/edit/remove within current session; exception is creating top-level skills directory which requires session restart.
claims.evidence: Live change detection section docs.

claims.claim: Nested discovery: in monorepo, editing file in packages/frontend/ also loads skills from packages/frontend/.claude/skills/.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'if you're editing a file in packages/frontend/, Claude Code also looks for skills in packages/frontend/.claude/skills/'.

claims.claim: --add-dir flag grants file access but not configuration, except skills: .claude/skills/ inside added directories loads automatically (unique exception among subagents/commands/output-styles).
claims.evidence: Docs on --add-dir behavior.

claims.claim: allowed-tools field pre-approves tools without permission prompt but does NOT restrict available tools; every tool remains callable via user permission settings.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'It does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable'.

claims.claim: Skills do NOT sync across surfaces: Claude Code (filesystem), claude.ai (zip upload), Claude API (/v1/skills endpoints) require separate management.
claims.evidence: Cross-surface limitations section docs.

claims.claim: Runtime environment differs by surface: Claude API has NO network access and NO runtime package install (pre-configured deps only); Claude Code has full host network but discourages global package install.
claims.evidence: Runtime section docs.

claims.claim: Claude Code skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io); core fields (name, description) portable across AI tools (OpenCode etc.); invocation control, subagent execution, and dynamic context injection are Claude Code extensions.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'Claude Code skills follow the Agent Skills open standard... Claude Code extends the standard with additional features'.

claims.claim: Anthropic bundles pre-built skills: Claude Code bundles /simplify, /batch, /debug, /loop, /claude-api; Claude API and claude.ai bundle pptx, xlsx, docx, pdf (container-based, Anthropic hosted); open-source repo github.com/anthropics/skills.
claims.evidence: Pre-built skills section docs.

claims.claim: Common installation error: nesting SKILL.md one level too deep. Correct path is ~/.claude/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md NOT ~/.claude/skills/skill-name/another-folder/SKILL.md.
claims.evidence: Quote: 'The most frequent installation error is nesting the skill one level too deep'.

conflicts_flagged.description: Description char cap: API spec (1024) vs Claude Code listing (1536 combined description+when_to_use). Not strictly contradictory (1024 per field, 1536 per combined entry), but behavior unclear when description alone exceeds 1024 on API upload.

user-invocable:false + disable-model-invocation:true combination: skill is menu-hidden AND auto-invocation-blocked AND Skill-tool-blocked. Docs do not explicitly state outcome; effectively zombie skill.

gaps_flagged.description: Skill chaining mechanism (skill invoking another skill) not explicitly documented. Indirect paths via context:fork + subagent-with-skills but direct chain unclear. Routed to R4.
Plugin skill vs same-named user skill: plugin gets namespace prefix but which wins when user types /name? Routed to R6.

Practical max-skills limit given 1% budget / 8000 char fallback / 1536 char per entry. Anthropic claims 40 skills = 1500 tokens but per-entry cap suggests ~5 skills fit in 8k. Discrepancy requires empirical test. Routed to R2.
Recursion: context:fork with agent that has skills: field itself. Docs silent on nested fork behavior.

summary: R1 establishes baseline: 4 scope levels, 13 frontmatter fields, 3-level progressive disclosure (~100/~5k/unlimited tokens), 3 invocation paths (auto/manual/Skill tool), 25k compaction budget with 5k per skill, 1%/8000 char listing budget. Agent Skills open standard with Claude Code extensions. Primary gaps on chaining (R4) and plugin semantics (R6).
